motions.purpose: Move attention between seven planets with a scale-and-fade crossfade while the fact panel updates to the selected planet's real values.
motions.model: Axial tilts and fact-panel values come from NASA planetary fact sheets; textures are Solar System Scope CC BY 4.0 photographic maps; the transition choreography is presentational.
motions.limitations: Planets render at unit radius, so sizes are not comparable; lighting is shared and illustrative; moon counts are approximate and change with discoveries.
motions.reducedMotion: The selected planet appears instantly with no crossfade; facts remain readable.
motions.exportState: Freeze on Mars with atmosphere and rings visible, stars hidden, controls hidden.
motions.accessibility: Planet buttons are native buttons; arrow keys switch planets inside the focused figure; all facts are text in the panel and caption.

motions.purpose: Give the gas giants living atmospheres: counter-rotating zonal bands with shear turbulence, Jupiter's Great Red Spot anticyclone, Saturn's north-polar hexagon and ring shadows, Neptune's transient dark spot and racing cirrus, and Galilean/Titan moons whose shadows transit the disc.
motions.model: Band structure alternates direction with latitude (real zonal-jet organization); GRS is a fixed-longitude vortex warp; the hexagon follows a six-fold polar boundary; moon periods use the real 1:2:4:9.4 Galilean ratios; moon and ring shadows are exact ray projections along the scene sun direction.
motions.limitations: Wind speeds, vortex strength, storm timing, and moon sizes/distances are display-scaled; cloud detail is texture warping, not fluid simulation.
motions.reducedMotion: Atmospheres and moons freeze at noise time 31.7 with shadows rendered at that instant.
motions.exportState: Same frozen tableau at time 31.7; deterministic seeded moon phases.
motions.accessibility: All dynamic phenomena are named in the caption as text; the moons toggle disables satellites and their shadows entirely.

motions.purpose: Give each planet a visible rotation whose relative rate follows its real day length — Jupiter visibly outpaces Venus.
motions.model: Visual spin rate is proportional to 24 hours divided by the planet's real rotation period, clamped for legibility; retrograde spin for Venus and Uranus emerges from their real axial tilts (177.4 and 97.8 degrees).
motions.limitations: Absolute speeds are sped up enormously for display; only the ordering and retrograde character are faithful.
motions.reducedMotion: Planets render as a fixed frame with no spin.
motions.exportState: Spin frozen at the mounted orientation.
motions.accessibility: Space pauses, Escape stops; the spin carries no information that the fact panel does not state as text.
